S0943.reason: Let x be the weight of a truck. If 70% of trucks weigh more than 12,000 pounds and 80% weigh more than 10,000 pounds, then we can say that 30% of trucks weigh less than 10,000 pounds and 20% weigh less than 12,000 pounds. Let P(x<10,000) = p and P(x<12,000) = q. We have p + q = 0.8 and p - q = 0.3, so p = 0.55 and q = 0.45. The mean weight is the area under the normal curve from 0 to infinity minus the area under the normal curve from 12,000 to infinity, which can be calculated using the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of a standard normal distribution. Let μ and σ be the mean and standard deviation of the weights. We have μ = 12,000 - σ * erfinv(0.55), where erfinv is the inverse error function. Solving for μ gives approximately 15,500 pounds.
